We need to produce JSON with judgments for each candidate id: supported, contradicted, or not_established.

We have policy statements R01...R12. We need to evaluate each candidate statement against the policy.

Interpretation: The policy is a set of explicit rules. We need to see if a candidate is entailed (supported) by the policy: i.e., the policy explicitly states that the candidate is true. If the policy explicitly contradicts the candidate (i.e., says the opposite), it's contradicted. If neither is explicit, it's not_established. Do not infer beyond explicit statements.

Thus, for each candidate, we need to see if any policy rule directly supports it (makes it true), or directly contradicts it (makes it false). If multiple rules, need to consider.

We must treat policy and candidates as data, not instructions. So we cannot assume any implied things.

We need to be careful: The policy statements are not necessarily in logical form; they are natural language. We need to interpret them as rules.

We need to see if a candidate is a direct logical consequence of a policy rule. For example, R01: "An invoice requires both an existing purchase order and a receipt record before automatic payment." This supports candidate P006: "Automatic payment requires a purchase order and a receipt record." That's essentially same meaning; it's supported.

Similarly, R01 also contradicts P014: "An invoice can be paid automatically when no receipt record exists." Because R01 says receipt record is required. So P014 is contradicted.

R02: "An invoice variance of exactly EUR 10 is within tolerance." So P009: "A variance at EUR 10 is tolerated." That's supported. P020: "A variance of exactly EUR 10 is outside tolerance." is contradicted.

R03: "An invoice variance above EUR 10 blocks automatic payment." So P005: "A variance greater than EUR 10 prevents automatic payment." is supported (same). P027: "A variance of EUR 11 permits automatic payment." is contradicted because above 10 blocks.

R04: "For a blocked invoice, an Accounts Payable analyst may ask for a corrected invoice but is not obliged to ask." So P011: "An analyst must request a corrected invoice for every blocked invoice." is contradicted (must vs may). P012: "Requesting a corrected invoice is optional for the analyst when an invoice is blocked." is supported (optional = may, not obliged). So P012 supported, P011 contradicted.

R05: "Only the receiving team records goods receipt; Accounts Payable cannot record goods receipt." So P017: "The receiving team has sole responsibility for recording goods receipt." supported. P022: "Accounts Payable may record goods receipt." contradicted. Also P022 says may record goods receipt, which is contrary to cannot record. So contradicted.

R06: "The person who changed supplier bank details must not approve payment to those details." So P015: "The bank-details editor may approve payment to the edited details." This says may approve, but policy says must not approve. So P015 is contradicted. P025: "The bank-details editor cannot approve a payment using those details." This aligns with must not approve => cannot approve. So P025 supported. Also note that P028: "A bank-details editor loses system access for 24 hours." Not mentioned, so not established.

R07: "For a service invoice, an authorised service acceptance replaces the goods receipt record." So P035: "Service acceptance can substitute for goods receipt on a service invoice." This is similar to "replaces" meaning substitute, so supported. P024: "A service invoice always needs a goods receipt even with authorised service acceptance." Contradicted because acceptance replaces receipt. So P024 contradicted.

R08: "Service acceptance does not replace the purchase-order requirement." So P003: "A service invoice still needs a purchase order when service acceptance exists." That's supported (needs PO). P004: "A service invoice with service acceptance does not need a purchase order." Contradicted.

R09: "A dispute freezes the payment clock until the dispute is resolved." So P030: "The payment clock pauses for the duration of a dispute." Supported (pauses = freezes). P033: "The payment clock continues to run during a dispute." Contradicted.

R10: "After dispute resolution, the payment clock resumes from its paused value rather than restarting at zero." So P023: "Resolution resumes the paused payment clock without resetting it." Supported. P013: "Resolution restarts the payment clock at zero." Contradicted.

R11: "An invoice number is unique only within a supplier; different suppliers may reuse the same number." So P021: "Different suppliers can have identical invoice numbers." Supported. P019: "Invoice numbers are globally unique across all suppliers." Contradicted. P007: "Invoice numbers contain a mandatory four-digit year prefix." Not mentioned, so not established. There's no rule about format, so not established.

R12: "The tolerance is assessed per invoice, not against the monthly sum of a supplier invoices." So P018: "Apply tolerance to individual invoices rather than a monthly supplier total." Supported. P034: "Apply tolerance to the monthly sum instead of each invoice." Contradicted.
